subject: Spark: [3/N] Support sending referenced-by to all endpoints (#13979)
body:
* Spark: Send the referenced-by view chain through SparkCatalog

Resolve the chain of views a relation was reached through and pass it to the
catalog as a LoadContext, so a REST catalog can forward it to the server.

SparkSupportsLoadContext extends the loading contract with context-carrying
overloads of loadTable and loadView, including the time-travel forms, and
SparkCatalog and SparkSessionCatalog implement it. ResolveViews records the
chain while resolving nested views, with UnResolvedRelationFromView carrying it
through analysis. Cross-catalog view references fail rather than silently
dropping the chain.

Gated behind spark.sql.iceberg.referenced-by-enabled, off by default.

* Spark: Move referenced-by context to Spark 4.2

Generated-by: Codex

* Spark: Fix ViewUtil Scala import grouping

Generated-by: Codex

* Spark 4.2: Implement contextual loadTable in TestSparkCatalog

TestSparkCatalog only overrode loadTable(Identifier), so once the read
path started resolving through loadRelation -> loadTable(Identifier,
LoadContext), the double was no longer consulted and lookups fell
through to the real catalog.

Override the contextual variant to delegate to the existing one. The
double ignores the context; TestReferencedByViewChain covers the
referenced-by behaviour against real catalogs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Spark 4.2: Restore explicit referenced-by view resolution

Restore the Spark 4.1-style analyzer path for referenced-by propagation in Spark 4.2. ResolveViews now expands Iceberg views, carries the view chain through UnResolvedRelationFromView, and loads nested relations with an explicit LoadContext instead of using SQLConf-backed view metadata.

Generated-by: Codex

* Core, Spark: Address referenced-by review feedback

Preserve existing cross-catalog view behavior by dropping catalog-relative referenced-by entries that cannot be represented for the target catalog. Bypass CachingCatalog for non-empty LoadContext loads so referenced-by reaches catalogs such as REST, and add regression coverage for cache-enabled Spark reads, time-travel views, and cross-catalog view references.

Generated-by: Codex

* Spark 4.2: Gate referenced-by view resolution

Add a default-off Spark SQL flag for referenced-by view-chain propagation. When disabled, Spark keeps its native view resolution behavior, including cross-catalog views. When enabled, Iceberg uses the explicit analyzer path and rejects cross-catalog chains because LoadContext carries catalog-relative identifiers.

Generated-by: Codex

* Spark 4.2: Use resolved view identity for referenced-by

Build the referenced-by view chain from the catalog and identifier Spark resolved when loading the view. Keep view metadata current catalog and namespace only for resolving unqualified references inside the view SQL.

Generated-by: Codex

* Spark 4.2: Address referenced-by review feedback

Keep the view chain on Spark's pre-execution table refresh by binding
it to the catalog of relations resolved through a view, so a table read
through a view is never reloaded as direct access. Convert view time
travel with Spark's TimeTravelSpec so string and integer timestamps work
and pinned snapshots are not refreshed. Leave V1 and delegating tables
read through a view to Spark, and alias view-resolved tables so
table-qualified columns resolve. Remove loadRelation overrides that
duplicate BaseCatalog.

* Spark 4.2: Resolve referenced-by views in a dedicated rule

Move referenced-by view expansion out of ResolveViews into
ResolveReferencedByViews, which does nothing when referenced-by is
disabled. ResolveViews is back to its main behavior.

With referenced-by enabled, BaseCatalog.loadRelation returns tables
only, so Spark resolves tables itself and leaves Iceberg views
unresolved for the new rule. This removes the hint-batch registration,
which Spark's Hive session state ignores, and keeps a table read to a
single load. Expanded views are wrapped in Spark's View node so cycle
detection and cache invalidation keep working, and parse, streaming and
not-found errors match Spark's.

LoadContext gains equals and hashCode so cached plans over a view are
reused by later queries.

SparkSessionCatalog fails a load with a referenced-by chain when its
Iceberg catalog cannot pass the context, instead of dropping it.

Generated-by: Claude Code

* Core, Spark 4.2: Bound referenced-by view depth and canonicalize contextual loads

Fail referenced-by view expansion past spark.sql.view.maxNestedViewDepth
with the same error Spark raises when referenced-by is disabled, so a
view cycle no longer overflows the stack during analysis.

CachingCatalog now sends contextual loads the same canonical identifier
as cached loads, so a table read through a view and read directly reach
the delegate under one name when the cache is case-insensitive.

Drop two Spark tests covered by more specific ones.

Generated-by: Claude Code

* Spark 4.2: Expand referenced-by views through SessionCatalog.getRelation

Referenced-by view expansion now uses the same Spark path as when the
flag is off, so view columns bind by name, every view schema mode is
honored, and the view text is parsed with the SQL configs stored at
CREATE VIEW. Previously columns were bound by position, which returned
wrong data after the underlying columns were reordered.

Tests that should behave the same with the flag on or off now run with
both settings and assert the expected outcome directly.

subject: Core: Add v4 TrackedFile write wrappers for leaf and root manifests (#18853)
body:
Adds reusable wrappers that write a TrackedFile, with the tracking
supplied by the writer, using the v4 tracked file schema.

The leaf wrapper accepts only data files and writes tracking as given so
unassigned sequence numbers and first row IDs are inherited on read,
rejecting null sequence numbers that cannot be inherited. The root
wrapper requires the tracking to carry a snapshot ID and writes the
sequence numbers, manifest min sequence number, and first row ID that
the spec requires in the root manifest, assigning the commit's values to
files added by the commit. Both project spec partitions to the union
partition type when writing, and write a null spec ID and partition for
files whose spec has no partition fields, as the v4 spec requires for
unpartitioned files.

Content stats are written through a view laid out by the manifest's
content stats type, so stats from any ContentStats implementation,
including stats adapted from DataFile metrics, are written at the
correct positions.

subject: Spark 4.1: Add per-task scanDuration metric (#17562)
body:
* Spark 4.1: Add per-task scanDuration metric

Iceberg reports scan bytes and file/manifest counts per task, but the only
timer in the metrics system is totalPlanningDuration, which measures
driver-side planning. There is no metric for how long a task spent actually
reading data, so a scan's throughput cannot be derived from Iceberg metrics
alone.

Add scanDuration: wall time a task spends in BaseReader.next(), accumulated
per call rather than per row so the timer costs nothing measurable relative
to the read. Emitted as TaskScanDuration from BatchDataReader and
RowDataReader, aggregated by ScanDuration, mirroring the existing
TotalPlanningDuration pair.

Values are nanoseconds: a single split can be read in well under a
millisecond, so a millisecond timer would round most per-task reads to zero.
ScanDuration formats the aggregate as ns/us/ms/s for the UI.

subject: Spark: Reject ExpireSnapshots action on v4 tables (#18999)
body:
* Spark: Reject ExpireSnapshots action on v4 tables

The Spark `ExpireSnapshots` action computes expired files through the
`all_manifests` metadata table, which is not supported for v4 tables. Guard
`ExpireSnapshotsSparkAction.expireFiles()` to reject v4 before the expiration
commit so the table is never partially mutated, reading refreshed metadata so a
stale handle cannot slip an already-upgraded v4 table through.

Only this Spark action is guarded; core and other-engine expiration stay
reachable on v4 (they read manifests directly, not metadata tables). The guard
is also best-effort against a concurrent v3 to v4 upgrade committed between the
check and RemoveSnapshots' own refresh; closing that race atomically would need
a core-level gate.

Retarget TestExpireSnapshotsAction to v2/v3, gate the expire-using
TestRewriteTablePaths tests to v2/v3 while keeping v4 coverage for the rest, and
add TestExpireSnapshotsActionV4 for the v4 ehavior.

* Spark: Limit this PR to Spark 4.2

Remove the 3.5/4.0/4.1 changes so this PR targets only the latest Spark
version; those versions will be backported in separate PRs.

* Address review feedback on expire-snapshots v4 tests

subject: Nessie: Check namespace existence at the ref HEAD in listNamespaces (#18035)
body:
listNamespaces(Namespace) mixed two commit points inside one method. The
parent namespace existence check called api.getContent().reference(getReference()),
which pins the request to the hash the client cached when it first resolved
the reference. The child listing right below it used withReference(api.getEntries()),
which sends only the branch name for a mutable reference so the server answers
from the HEAD of the ref. A client that had not seen a newer commit therefore
got NoSuchNamespaceException for a namespace another client had just created,
even though the child listing would have found it.

Use the withReference(api.getContent()) idiom for the existence check so both
halves of the method read the same commit. loadNamespaceMetadata() in the same
class already reads namespace content that way.

The three remaining api.getContent().reference(getReference()) calls in this
class (createNamespace, dropNamespace, updateProperties) are left alone. They
are pre-checks that run right before a commit against that same hash, so
pinning the hash there is the intended behavior.

* Nessie: Reword test comment and use containsExactly in TestMultipleClients

Review follow-up for listNestedNamespacesFromAnotherClient. The first
listNamespaces() call does not pin the other client to a hash; it only
forces the client to resolve its reference before the commits below so
the hash it caches is older than those commits. Say that instead of
"pins", and use containsExactly since the listing has a single entry.
